rows.what the ink shows: The initial p has a low dipping stem, followed by a tall angular l; the compressed middle run ends in a descending g hook and short e stroke.
A small open initial a is followed by two separated low n strokes, a small e mark and the longer joined au finish.
Between trace and continue the first low n hook, small detached o mark and short final n stroke form the three-letter group non.
After un, a detached initial a mark precedes two low n strokes; the small open e and final looped a with trailing u remain visible.
Several angular remnants survive before the phi, but dense cancellation covers the numeral body and the putative plus crossing; 1+ cannot be separated securely.
Below phi there is one capital A with two oblique legs and a crossbar, flanked by a separate left upright and a dark right upright; cancellation thickens the right bar.
Inside the two parenthesis strokes, a single upright extends above and below the horizontal crossing. Its t crossbar is partly merged with the cancellation.
The parenthesis encloses a crossed tall t, a separate plus with vertical and horizontal arms, and one small closed oval zero.
The first word has the looped s, low e/c connections and final rising d; the second has compressed m shoulders, a tall b and short re ending.
The word after à begins with a distinctly crossed t, then a high r entry descending into the compressed ace run before the equals sign.
The superscript position is covered by a dense rectangular cancellation. No independent vertical and horizontal plus arms can be recovered from that patch.
At and immediately beside the blacked-out superscript there is no securely separable replacement dash; the short internal horizontal remnants belong to the obscured patch.
The deletion leaves a broad curved initial remnant, low connecting ink and a tall later stem, but its heavy horizontal stroke obscures the O/n and v/o boundaries needed to verify the whole phrase.
The canceled capital retains an upright left stem and distinct upper, middle and lower rightward bars; the bottom bar extends farther right.

The letter has a long rising left shoulder, two narrow joined loops and a right downstroke, like the H in the preceding X′ definition. The nearby X has opposing curved arms and a transverse join instead.
A looped left point opens into separate upper-right and lower-right arms. There is no separate lower wavy or horizontal stroke for lesssim.
A short initial i stroke is followed by a low connector, a deep p/l turn and the descending q-shaped turn before the short final e. The same-page impliquerait has the same initial connected turns.
Under the crossing strokes, a curved left parenthesis, central upright t and closing bowed stroke remain distinguishable. The cancellation overlaps the t crossbar.
The right-hand deleted group retains a separate curved opening stroke, a central tall t with a transverse stroke and a right closing hook. Diagonal deletion strokes cross the middle.
The small leading glyph has a bent upper stroke descending to a short rightward foot. It has no second diagonal crossing through its middle as x would.
The radical’s low check and long rising arm survive at the left. The following A-like diagonals are merged with broad cancellation strokes, so the radicand cannot be secured.
Crossing strokes cover the putative A, membership curve and right-hand looped letter. Several upright and curved remnants survive, but their boundaries and a distinct underline are obscured.
The word begins with a long p down-and-up turn, continues through a low connected middle with an i dot, and ends in a tall f with a descending stem. Its upper end touches the deleted note above.
In the rotated margin, a long initial p descender leads into a low joined r/e group; two small rises and a final trailing e stroke complete preuve. There is no extra separately written word.

The first inserted glyph has a broad open cup and a central stem extending above and below its junction. No upper closing stroke is visible, so its form does not securely distinguish the proposed phi variants; it is also psi-shaped.
The second inserted glyph has a shallow upturned bowl crossed by a tall central stem, with no closed oval. Its especially flat cup leaves the phi variants unresolved and permits a psi-shaped reading.
The lower-right index has a separate initial 1 and plus, then a single A between two upright bars. The A’s center is overtraced, but both legs and its surrounding bars remain visible.

An accented capital É is followed by the descending q turn and an open c; the connected continuation has dotted i strokes, crossed t forms and a final accented ending. The long middle connectors compress several letters.
The initial f has a tall down-and-return stroke; the compressed middle reaches a crossed t and dotted i, then a low connected ending with a separate terminal s hook.

A is clear below the cancellation, with two oblique legs and a crossbar. Above it a short horizontal stroke ends in a right hook, but overlapping loops and the deletion conceal the arrow construction.

Under the deletion, fonction retains a long f stem and a later crossed t with its following i dot; the final separate de has a raised d stroke and low trailing e. Several connecting bodies are flattened by the crossing line.
A short upright bends into a long low rightward exit, giving the compressed l-e sequence before the separately descending p of prouver.
The word begins with a closed q bowl and descending return; a small raised u shoulder leads into the low e exit, although the join is heavily retraced.
The first d has a tall stem with a hooked lower bowl, followed by an open-loop e; after the space a separate upright l hooks into a short e exit.

The upper a after A and the membership sign is a compact low oval with a rightward exit and no separate stroke beneath it. The nearby crossed-out lower a visibly has a distinct short underline, unlike this occurrence.
A tall initial P has an upper right bowl; the following low strokes and dots form the compressed r-e-n-o-n sequence, ending in a distinct right-facing s hook.

The initial e loop and tall crossed t survive, followed by a tall l and a small separated apostrophe. Cancellation covers the counters and joins of on; the last a retains its own raised hook and low rounded return.

A tall descending p and a small following shoulder remain above and below the cancellation. Several separated lower remnants extend to the right, leaving the short pour and longer prouver readings in competition.
The measure letter has a long descending left stem and a separate raised right shoulder, without a closed upper oval; the lower index strokes begin distinctly to its right.
The second letter again has a long left descent with an open right shoulder and short right return. Its shape is separate from the lower adjacent index and supports mu.

Before the integral there is a round upper mark and a displaced horizontal dash, so two equals bars are not secure. The integral, first baseline x with raised looped p, d and descending mu, two index bars enclosing one A, then parenthesized baseline x with a second raised p remain distinguishable despite the deletion.
